title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-21
korean_summary: 토요일 핵심: 회계장 CM 변경 사유 검토 후 승인 여부 결정, 커팅기 부품 견적 비교 후 구매요청 지시, 영업부 비용 마감. 응급처치 교육 시간·창고 교육계획 회신.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Saturday, November twenty-first. It is the last working day of this week. Next Tuesday is a paid holiday, so next week is short. Let's get ready together.

Here is the plan for the next twenty minutes. There are eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three tasks for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.

First, some good news from yesterday. You sent the forecast from November to February to head office on Friday afternoon. That deadline is done. You also decided not to buy a new PC for the QA team. The IT staff will set up an unused PC instead. Well done.
Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The chief accountant's reasons for the CM changes.

What is it? This is about the chief accountant. Last week she sent a new CM plan for November and December. CM means cutting and making, our sewing fee. In the new plan, the tax CM went up for several lines. On Thursday, you said you would not approve it yet. You asked for the reason for each style. Yesterday afternoon, she replied.

Her main point is simple. The export quantity for November and December went up a lot. If we keep the old tax CM, revenue drops too much. Then we cannot reach the profit target. She also explained each style. For example, one style was a repeat order, so there is no change. Another style moved from December to November, so it must use the November price.

Why does it matter? These lines are on hold. She cannot issue invoices until you approve. Shipments are going out next week. Also, you asked her to always get your approval before changing a plan. This is a good time to set that rule clearly.

Your first action today: read her reasons line by line, and check that the numbers add up. Then decide. Approve, or ask one or two more questions. Also note one thing. She said the final contract appendix does not exist yet. It is printed only after all orders are shipped. So you may need to change what you asked for.
Number two. The cutting machine repair in the CAD room.

What is it? The CAD room cutting machine needs two parts: a signal cable and a cushion strip. The IT staff got a second quotation yesterday, as you asked. Now there are two suppliers. The new supplier is much cheaper in total. Their parts price is much lower, but their installation fee is higher.
Why does it matter? You asked for the comparison by today, and it came one day early. The machine works now, but the old cable may fail again. The worn cushion strip can damage the blade.

Your first action today: check that both quotes cover the same parts. The new supplier put the cushion strip inside the cable line, because it has no separate code. Ask the CAD leader if the parts are the same. If yes, tell the IT staff to make the purchase request, PR for short, with the cheaper supplier.
Number three. The sales team DEBIT closing.
What is it? Today is the closing day for the sales team DEBIT. DEBIT is the monthly cost we charge to the head office sales team. Your calendar has an all-day reminder for this.
Why does it matter? On Monday, you need to submit the approval document in the groupware. If the numbers are not closed today, Monday will be a rush. And Tuesday is a holiday.
Your first action today: check that all sales team costs for this month are in the file. Ask the accounting team if any invoice is still missing.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, from the chief accountant. You asked her to send the tax CM calculation for these styles by today. Check that the calculation matches her reasons. You can say: "Could you send me the tax CM calculation file by noon? I want to finish my review today."

Second, from the import and export manager. She owed you three things by yesterday for the trucking contract: the original appendix, the insurance certificates from the trucking companies, and the maximum cargo value. Check if they came in. If not, you can say: "It has been a day since the deadline, and I still have not received the documents. Could you let me know where they stand?"

Also from the import and export manager: good news. She fixed the ledger points yesterday, one day early. The export rows now have the container type. Please check the file once and close this item. You can say: "Thank you for fixing it early. I checked the ledger, and it looks clear."

Third, from the HR staff. She was going to give her legal review on one worker's indefinite contract by today. One sewer's contract also ends today. Check the plan with her before the end of the day. You can say: "My understanding is that her contract ends today. Please correct me if I'm wrong. What is the plan for Monday?"

Fourth, from the warehouse. The warehouse manager said a detailed two-week training schedule for the new Statistic staff will come by email. You can say: "Please send me the day-by-day schedule, with who teaches each part."

Fifth, from the IT staff. He is setting up the unused PC for a QA staff member, withdrawing the PR, and updating the asset register. You can say: "Please let me know once the PC is ready and the register is updated."
Part four. Replies I owe.

Reply one. The compliance staff. She wants to hold first aid training on December fifth, in the showroom, for the staff on the list. It takes ninety minutes with an outside trainer. The old certificates expired on October fourth. She asks you to pick a time, and she says it can be during overtime hours. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for arranging this. Since the certificates already expired, let's not wait. Let's do it during overtime hours, so production is not affected." Check the production plan before you pick the exact time.

Reply two. The warehouse manager. She sent the daily task list and the two-week training plan. The list has many tasks a day, which is a lot for a new person. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you. The main reason new staff leave early is that the job is hard to learn. So for the first week, could she focus on only a few tasks?"

Reply three. The IT staff, about the cutting machine. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for the second quote. We'd like to go ahead with the cheaper supplier, provided that the parts are the same."
Reply four. The chief accountant, about the CM plan. Your first sentence could be: "Thank you for the detailed reasons. I'm not in a position to approve until I check the calculation file."
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.
Today, Saturday: the sales team DEBIT closing, the cutting machine quote, and the chief accountant's documents. One sewer's contract also ends today.
Monday, November twenty-third: The weekly firewood report for head office. The DEBIT approval document in the groupware. And a head office manager expects a courier import status.

Tuesday, November twenty-fourth: Vietnam Culture Day. It is a paid holiday for everyone. Also, our collective labor agreement expires that day. Check with the HR manager that the renewal is registered.
Wednesday, November twenty-fifth: a shipment leaves by sea. Also, from last month's rule, the chief accountant should send the December CM plan by the twenty-fifth.
Part six. English review.
Let's review expressions from yesterday, two days ago, four days ago, and last week.

The expression is "I'm not in a position to ... until ..." It means you cannot do something yet, because a step is missing. For example, "I'm not in a position to approve the plan until you explain each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I'm not in a position to approve the plan until you explain each style.
... ... ...

The expression is "should add up to." It means the parts should match the total. For example, "The amounts in the note column should add up to the total difference." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The amounts should add up to the total difference.
... ... ...

The expression is "rationale." It means the reason behind a decision. For example, "Please explain the rationale for the CM change for each style." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please explain the rationale for each style.
... ... ...

The expression is "Apart from ..., is there anything else ...?" It means you want to know about other things too. For example, "Apart from this list, is there anything else that was sent under our tax code?" Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Apart from this list, is there anything else?
... ... ...

The expression is "itemize." It means to list costs one by one. For example, "Please ask the suppliers to itemize the pump and installation costs." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please ask the suppliers to itemize the costs.
... ... ...

The expression is "To meet ...'s deadline of ..., please ... by ..." It means you set an earlier deadline to meet a bigger one. For example, "To meet head office's deadline of Monday, please send me the file by three PM today." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. To meet head office's deadline of Monday, please send me the file by three PM today.
... ... ...

The expression is "reimburse." It means to pay back money someone spent. For example, "Workers pay first, and the company reimburses them later." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The company reimburses them later.
... ... ...

The expression is "comparable." It means two things can be compared, because the conditions are the same. For example, "Please get comparable quotes for the same parts." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please get comparable quotes for the same parts.
... ... ...

The expression is "Unless I hear otherwise by ..., I will ..." It means you will act if nobody says no. For example, "Unless I hear otherwise by three PM, I will approve the purchase request." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise by three PM, I will approve it.
... ... ...

The expression is "From now on, let's make it a rule that ..." It means you set a new rule for the future. For example, "From now on, let's make it a rule that any change to an approved plan comes to me first." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. From now on, let's make it a rule that any change comes to me first.
... ... ...
Part seven. Role-play.
This morning, you will talk with the chief accountant, about her reasons for the CM changes. Listen first.
Anthony: Good morning. Thank you for your detailed reply yesterday.
Accountant: Good morning, Anthony. Did you have time to read it?
Anthony: Yes. Your main point is that the export quantity went up. If we keep the old tax CM, the profit rate goes above the target. Is that right?
Accountant: Yes, that's right. So I had to change some styles.
Anthony: I understand. But I'm not in a position to approve until I see the calculation file. The amounts should add up to the new total.
Accountant: I will send the file this morning.
Anthony: Thank you. Apart from these several lines, is there anything else that changed from the approved plan?
Accountant: No, only these several lines.
Anthony: Good. One more thing. You said the contract appendix is only final after shipping. Then please send me the draft appendix instead.
Accountant: Okay, I can send the draft.
Anthony: From now on, if you need to change an approved plan, please tell me first. Unless I hear otherwise by noon, I will review the file this afternoon.
Accountant: Understood. Thank you, Anthony.
Here is a second short talk. Later this morning, you call the IT staff about the cutting machine.
Anthony: Hi there. Thank you for the second quote. It came one day early.
IT staff: You're welcome, Anthony. The new supplier is much cheaper.
Anthony: Yes. But I want to make sure the quotes are comparable. The new supplier put the cushion strip inside the cable line. Is it the same part?
IT staff: They said it is the same. They just have no separate code for it.
Anthony: Okay. Please ask the CAD leader to check the part number with you. If it is the same, please make the PR with the new supplier.
IT staff: Sure. I will check with the CAD leader today.
Anthony: Great. And please ask them to itemize the cushion strip in the final invoice, so that accounting can check it.
IT staff: No problem.
Now let's practice two key sentences from the first talk.

First sentence. I'm not in a position to approve until I see the calculation file.
... ... ...
One more time. I'm not in a position to approve until I see the calculation file.
... ... ...

Second sentence. Apart from these several lines, is there anything else that changed?
... ... ...
One more time. Apart from these several lines, is there anything else that changed?
... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.
Here is the one thing to remember today. Check the chief accountant's calculation, then decide on the CM plan, so the invoices are not held over the holiday.
Also, close the DEBIT numbers, and tell the IT staff which supplier to use for the cutting machine.
You finished the big head office report this week. Have a good rest on Sunday. See you on Monday.
